reply: {"verses": [], "overall": "The translation follows the Latin closely in every verse: tenses (fundatur present passive, cognoscetur and reget future, conteres future second person), voices and persons are kept, the Septuagintal readings (latera Aquilonis, cum suscipiet eam, distribuite domos ejus) are preserved rather than smoothed toward the Hebrew, and nothing is added or dropped. 'Quando a amparar' for 'cum suscipiet eam' is a fair rendering of suscipere as upholding/taking under protection. Pointing marks match the Latin in every verse (a single mediant each)."}
